newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz - car thefts still falling in 97.
newsitem.headline: Allianz - car thefts still falling in 97.

text.p: The incidence of car theft continued to drop in Germany at the start of 1997, Allianz AG Holding's domestic non-life unit said on Tuesday.

Improved electronic locking devices had already helped thefts of Allianz-insured cars to drop to 11,362 in 1996 from 14,920 the previous year, Allianz Versicherungs AG board mamber Friedrich Caspers told a news conference.
In 1994, 18,183 car thefts were registered and 19,037 were stolen in 1993.
Allianz said 550,000 cars insured with it had been fitted with new electronic locks in 1996 and only 223 of these had been reported stolen.
The insurer also noted that stolen cars were increasingly being moved further eastward than the former major markets for stolen German vehicles, Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
